title: ck or k?
rule: At the end of a word, look at the ONE letter right before the k sound. A short vowel alone: spell it ck. A consonant or a vowel team: spell it k.
trickText: Look at the ONE letter right before the k sound. Not the whole word, just that one letter. Short vowel, all alone? Use c k. Consonant or vowel team? Use just k.
say: Today's case: c k or k. Here is the trick. Do not look at the whole word. Look at the ONE letter right before the k sound. If it is a short vowel all alone, use c k. If it is a consonant or a vowel team, use just k.

example.say: Look at black. The one letter right before the k sound is a. It is a short vowel, all alone. So we spell it c k. Black.

activities.instruction: Find the ONE letter before the k sound. Then choose c k or k.

discover.intro: Sort these words by how they end: c k, or just k.
discover.question: Look at the ONE letter right before the ending. In black, duck and stick, what is it?
discover.reveal: Yes! A short vowel alone gets c k. After a consonant, like milk and park, or a vowel team, like cheek, we use just k.
